probe.area: us-fundamentals: point-in-time US fundamentals from SEC XBRL companyfacts (keyless). Probe set: 10 current names (AAPL 320193, MSFT 789019, NVDA 1045810, JPM 19617, XOM 34088+2115436, JNJ 200406, WMT 104169, KO 21344, GOOGL 1288776+1652044, PG 80424) and 10 delisted or acquired names (ATVI 718877, TWTR 1418091, XLNX 743988, CELG 816284, RHT 1087423, AGN 1578845 [Allergan plc, ex-Actavis; before 2015 the AGN ticker was Allergan Inc 850693], MON 1110783, TWX 1105705, LLTC 791907, SHLD 1310067). Everything was run on 2026-09-25. Scripts and caches are in scratch/pit/us-fundamentals/. The main module is pit_us_fund.py and the end-to-end example is run_pit.py. Outputs are pit_panel_20names.csv (3,760 month-end rows x 27 columns) and pit_events_20names.csv (1,067 filing-date rows). The repo was not modified; quantcio.data.us is only imported.

working.name: pit_us_fund.py: CompanyFacts, pit_quarterly, pit_instant, snapshot_features, pit_feature_events, month_end_panel, detect_splits_xbrl, splits_series
working.purpose: Builds PIT quarterly series and month-end features from companyfacts JSON. It reuses quantcio quarterly_series and ttm_series (YTD-to-quarter derivation, unit pick, form filter, per-fact split adjustment) and adds four things: 1) multi-CIK merge; 2) per-filing concept coalescing (revenue takes the max over total-revenue concepts in the same filing, with goods+services as a fallback; NI and EPS use priority order); 3) as-of snapshots, where at filing date d only facts with filed<=d are visible and each period takes the latest value filed<=d; 4) the features TTM EPS, P/E, P/B, ROE, operating margin and revenue YoY (quarter and TTM), usable from filed+1 day.
working.output_shape: pit_quarterly -> quantcio quarterly_series frame [start, end, value, yoy, qoq, derived, concept, unit, form, accn, filed, first_filed]. pit_instant -> [end, val, filed, prio, concept, unit, accn]. pit_feature_events -> one row per filing date: [asof, q_end, rev_q, rev_yoy_q, ttm_rev, ttm_ni, ttm_op, ttm_eps, eps_src (xbrl_eps|xbrl_fy_eps|ni/shares), rev_yoy_ttm, op_margin, equity, equity_src, roe, shares, shares_src (dei_cover|bs_shares|wavg_diluted), shares_implied, bvps, q_derived, available=asof+1d]. month_end_panel -> one row per month-end: date plus the event columns (merge_asof on available<=date; features NaN if q_end is more than 200 days old), and close, pe, ey, pb, bm when a price is given. Per-share values are on today's split basis.
working.coverage: Month-end, inside each name's listed window (2,902 month-ends). Current names averaged: ttm_eps 99.8%, P/E 99.2%, P/B 99.8%, ROE 100%, op_margin 72.1% (JPM 0, XOM 0, JNJ 20.7: those filers do not tag OperatingIncomeLoss), rev_yoy_q 95.3% (XOM 53.2), rev_yoy_ttm 94.7%, bvps 99.8%. Delisted names averaged: ttm_eps 96.6% (TWTR 88.3 and LLTC 90.5, from the first-year TTM ramp), ROE 91.3% (SHLD 52.1, negative equity), op_margin 96.4%, rev_yoy_q 99.4%, rev_yoy_ttm 96.4%, bvps 99.8%. P/E and P/B are 0% for delisted names because there is no keyless price source (see failing). EPS source across the 1,067 events: xbrl_eps 743, xbrl_fy_eps 262, ni/shares 17. Share source: dei_cover 998, bs_shares 62, wavg_diluted 6.
working.notes:
Checked by hand against the filing documents, fetched and cleaned with quantcio parse_filing_index and edgar_html_to_text in p9_verify.py.

AAPL at 2019-02-28 (as of the 10-Q filed 2019-01-30):
- Every value matches the filings exactly: q revenue 84,310 vs 88,293 a year earlier (YoY -4.51%), TTM revenue 261,612, TTM operating income 67,970 (Q4 FY18 derived as FY 70,898 - 9M 54,780 = 16,118), op margin 0.2598, TTM NI 59,431, equity 117,892 vs 140,199 a year earlier (ROE 0.4605).
- TTM diluted EPS 12.16/4 = 3.04 and cover shares 4,715,280,000 x 4 match. P/E = 43.2875/3.04 = 14.24.

CELG at 2019-03-31 (FY2018 10-K): revenue 15,281, operating income 5,191, NI 4,046, equity 6,161 vs 6,921 (ROE 0.6186) and cover shares 702,164,345 all match. Summing quarterly EPS gave 5.53 against the reported 5.51, so a fix was added: at a fiscal-year end the reported FY EPS is used (now 5.51; AAPL FY18 gives 11.91/4 = 2.9775).

Speed: 1.42 s per company on average (max 2.1 s) for 26 to 70 events; 28 s in total for 20 names.

working.name: secnet.py: polite SEC fetcher with gzip disk cache
working.purpose: Keyless SEC GETs at 4 req/s or less with the required User-Agent. It asks for gzip transfer and keeps a gzip disk cache. companyfacts() and submissions() are wrappers.
working.output_shape: bytes / dict (raw companyfacts JSON: facts[ns][concept].units[unit] = [{start?, end, val, accn, fy, fp, form, filed, frame?}])
working.coverage: 22/22 companyfacts fetches returned 200 and 86/86 submissions pages returned 200. No 403 or 429 errors.
working.notes: Measured per companyfacts: body mean 3.18 MB (median 3.01, max 7.96 for JPM), 0.217 MB on the wire with gzip (about 7%), latency mean 0.57 s (max 1.92 s).

working.name: detect_splits_xbrl (XBRL-only stock-split detection)
working.purpose: Recovers split events for delisted names (Yahoo has no data for them) from re-filed EPS ratios, checked against the jump in the dei cover share count.
working.verified_code:
det = detect_splits_xbrl(CompanyFacts.from_json({816284: secnet.companyfacts(816284)}))
# CELG -> window_lo 2014-04-29, window_hi 2014-07-29, ratio 2, n 9, share_count_confirms True
splits = splits_series(det)   # Series({2014-07-29: 2.0}) -> pass as `splits`
working.coverage: All 8 real splits since 2009 were found: AAPL 2014 7:1 and 2020 4:1, NVDA 2021 4:1 and 2024 10:1, WMT 2024 3:1, KO 2012 2:1, GOOGL 2014 ~2:1 class-C dividend and 2022 20:1, CELG 2014 2:1. Each window contained Yahoo's split date, and there were 0 false positives across the 20 names. share_count_confirms was True for 6 and None for GOOGL, which has no dei cover count.
working.notes: Use window_hi (the first filing on the new basis) as the split date for split_factor_after. The true date lies inside (window_lo, window_hi], which is 2-3 months wide, so an UNADJUSTED price source for a delisted name needs its own split dates.

failing.name: quantcio quarterly_series with extra concepts
failing.error: quarterly_series(facts, metric) only reads XBRL_CONCEPTS[metric] (e.g. eps_diluted = [EarningsPerShareDiluted, EarningsPerShareBasicAndDiluted]), so any other concept in the dict is silently ignored. PG's FY2014 10-Qs tag only IncomeLossFromContinuingOperationsPerDilutedShare, which left TTM EPS NaN for 10 months (2013-10 to 2014-07).
failing.workaround: pit_us_fund._coalesce merges each metric's concepts per filing and re-keys them under XBRL_CONCEPTS[metric][0]. PG ttm_eps is now 100%. The repo module was not changed.

probe.recommended_design:
Recommended construction:

1. CIK chains. Keep a dated table of ticker -> [CIK chain]. company_tickers.json covers current names; delisted names come from EDGAR autocomplete plus submissions (formerNames, 25-NSE date). Predecessor CIKs are required, e.g. Google Inc -> Alphabet, XOM 34088 -> 2115436, and AGN = Allergan Inc 850693 until 2015-03 then Allergan plc 1578845. Fetch companyfacts once per CIK and cache the trimmed concept subset (0.28 MB JSON / 0.017 MB gz per company).

2. Build CompanyFacts. Keep only 10-K/10-Q forms and their amendments. Coalesce concepts per filing:
   - Revenue = max over the total-revenue concepts in the same filing (Revenues, RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax, SalesRevenueNet, ...), otherwise goods + services. No single revenue concept covers more than about 55% of quarters, while the combination covers 96-100%. In the same filing, RevenueFromContract is 0.95-0.99x Revenues at XOM, WMT and CELG, and PG's FY12-14 10-K tags 'Revenues' as 28.4B vs SalesRevenueNet 82.0B. A fixed priority order therefore gets the wrong total; max is right in every conflict observed.
   - NI and EPS use priority order, with continuing-ops EPS as the last fallback.

3. As-of snapshots. For every distinct filing date d (about 4-6 per year), build the snapshot from facts with filed <= d, taking the LATEST value filed <= d per period. Derive quarters with quantcio quarterly_series and TTM with ttm_series. At a fiscal-year end, use the reported FY EPS. Instants (equity, shares) follow the same rule. Equity is StockholdersEquity, else total equity minus MinorityInterest. Shares come from the dei cover count, then CommonStockSharesOutstanding, then diluted weighted average, each sanity-checked against the NI/EPS-implied count. Mark each event available = filed + 1 day, then merge_asof to month-ends and set values to NaN when the quarter is more than 200 days old.

4. Prices. Use split-adjusted, NOT dividend-adjusted closes. Put per-share values on today's basis: EPS divided by the splits after the fact's filed date; the cover share count multiplied by the splits after its as-of date. Split events come from Yahoo for current names and from detect_splits_xbrl for delisted names.

5. Store both panels. Keep the event table and the month-end panel, and prefer ey and bm (defined for losses) over pe and pb as model inputs.

Why the as-of rule matters: every restatement enters on its own filing date, never earlier.
- JPM Q1-2012 NI is 5.383B from 2012-05-10 until the 10-Q/A on 2012-08-09, then 4.924B.
- AAPL FY2009 EPS is 6.29 until the 10-K/A on 2010-01-25 (9.08 after).
- The naive build that quantcio.trailing_pe_history uses (latest value dated at first_filed) differs from as-of by more than 0.5% at 15.0% (revenue), 11.6% (NI) and 10.5% (EPS) of month-ends, and by more than 5% at 6.6%, 4.6% and 4.0%. That is look-ahead.
- A first-vintage-only build is also PIT-safe but ignores recasts that were already public. It differs from as-of by more than 0.5% at 5.0%, 6.4% and 5.3% of month-ends.

Residual biases and how to measure them:
(a) Clock conservatism. The 10-Q/10-K filed date lags the 8-K Item 2.02 earnings release by a median of 5 days (p95 22) for 10-Q and 20 days (p95 41) for 10-K. 99.5% of periodic filings have a preceding 2.02 8-K. To measure: rebuild with available = the 8-K 2.02 date and compare the IC decay of earnings-based signals.
(b) Structural missingness. XOM revenue 2011-16, op income at banks, energy names and JNJ, multi-class EPS (GOOGL 2015-18). To measure: coverage by sector and size bucket by month. Rank features within the available set rather than filling them. SEC Financial Statement Data Sets can recover custom-tag gaps.
(c) XBRL phase-in. Large caps have first_filed 2009-07 to 2010-11; smaller filers only from mid-2011, and their TTM starts about 4 quarters later (LLTC TTM from 2011-08, XLNX from 2011-06). To measure: monthly coverage by size bucket; start the backtest in 2012 or require a TTM.
(d) Derived-quarter error. Within-year TTM EPS still includes one FY-minus-9M derived quarter (CELG 5.53 vs 5.51 = 0.4%), and the NI/shares proxy has a median error of 2.1%. To measure: compare to FY EPS at fiscal-year ends.
(e) Tagging errors in originals are faithfully reproduced. Example: AGN 2013Q3 OperatingIncomeLoss = 970, later 155.7M. 7.33% of re-filed fact versions change the value (10-Q/A 33.7%, 10-K/A 3.1%, later 10-Q 7.4%, later 10-K 6.9%). To measure: flag monetary values below 1e4 USD for companies with more than 1e8 revenue, and winsorize.
(f) companyfacts staleness (1/1,078 filings: KO 2026-07-29). To measure: nightly accession diff against submissions.
(g) Survivorship. It lives in the universe, not in the fundamentals: the 10 delisted names have 96-100% fundamental coverage. The missing piece is a delisted price source for P/E and P/B.

Filing lag, period end -> filing date (from submissions): 10-Q median 32 days (p5 20, p95 39, p99 40); 10-K median 49 (p5 29, p95 59, p99 61, max 75). Fact level: direct quarters median 32 days (p95 57); derived Q4 median 50.5 (p95 59). 2.0% of quarters become public only through later comparatives, more than 100 days after period end (AGN 22, TWTR 12 pre-IPO, SHLD 6, GOOGL 5).
probe.full_build_estimate:
For about 700 CIKs plus about 5-10% predecessor CIKs:

- companyfacts: about 750 requests. On the wire about 0.22 MB each (gzip), so about 165 MB. Raw JSON is 3.18 MB each on average (max 7.96 MB), about 2.4 GB, which should not be kept; the trimmed cache is about 200 MB JSON or 12 MB gz.
- Fetch time: at the measured 0.57 s mean latency, one thread takes about 7 minutes; 3 threads capped at 5 req/s take about 2.5 minutes.
- submissions (dates, 25-NSE, reportDate), optional: the probe needed 86 requests for 22 CIKs (about 3.9 per CIK, skipping pages with filingTo < 2009). That is about 2,700 requests, 9-10 minutes at 5 req/s, and about 200 MB.
- Yahoo prices for current names: 1 request per ticker.
- Compute: pit_feature_events takes 1.42 s per company on average (max 2.1 s) for 26-70 filing events. That is about 17 minutes on one core, or about 3 minutes with 8 processes. The month-end panel step is negligible.
- Total for a full 2011-2026 build: under 20 minutes wall time and under 400 MB downloaded. The request count does not depend on the number of years, because companyfacts is one request per CIK covering all history.
- Bulk alternative (all ~19k filers, no per-request limits): companyfacts.zip 1,409 MB and submissions.zip 1,565 MB, both Last-Modified 2026-09-24.
- Daily incremental: refetch companyfacts only for CIKs with a new 10-K/10-Q in submissions (about 5-40 per day in earnings season).
gotchas: Use the filing date (first_filed / filed) as the PIT clock, never the period end, fy/fp or frame. XBRL fy/fp describe the filing, not the fact. Add +1 day because filings land after the close.

quantcio trailing_pe_history / quarterly_series(vintage='latest') pair a restated value with the ORIGINAL first_filed date, which is look-ahead. In this probe that changes month-end TTM by more than 0.5% at 10-15% of month-ends (more than 5% at 4-7%). For backtests, use as-of snapshots (filter filed <= t, then take the latest).

Amendments are real and material. AAPL FY2009 10-K/A (2010-01-25): revenue 36.537B -> 42.905B, EPS 6.29 -> 9.08. JPM Q1-2012 10-Q/A (2012-08-09): NI 5.383B -> 4.924B, EPS 1.31 -> 1.19. MON had 6 amendments (2011-11-14). 10-Q/A re-filings change a value 33.7% of the time.

No single revenue concept covers more than ~55% of quarters: Revenues 50% (current) / 53% (delisted), RevenueFromContract 34% / 17%, SalesRevenueNet 21% / 37%. KO and JNJ before 2018 tag only SalesRevenueGoodsNet. Fixed priority orders pick subsets: RevenueFromContract < Revenues at XOM, WMT and CELG; PG's FY12-14 'Revenues' is 28.4B vs SalesRevenueNet 82.0B. Take the max per filing.
OperatingIncomeLoss is structurally absent for banks and energy (JPM, XOM) and for JNJ after 2015. XOM's quarterly revenue 2011-2016 is not in companyfacts, probably custom tags.

Multi-class filers (GOOGL): companyfacts drops dimensional facts. Alphabet has no dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding and no non-dimensional EPS in its original 2015-2018 10-Qs. Fall back to CommonStockSharesOutstanding and NI/shares.

dei cover share counts are AS OF the cover date, so apply splits after 'end'. Financial-statement per-share values and share counts are restated for splits before filing, so apply splits after 'filed'.
The Q4 EPS derived as FY - 9M ignores share-count drift (CELG TTM 5.53 vs reported 5.51). Use the reported FY EPS at fiscal-year ends.
companyfacts can silently miss a recent filing (KO 10-Q 2026-07-29, still missing about 8 weeks later) even though frames has it. Diff accessions against submissions.
The frames API is latest-vintage only (it returns the restated JPM Q1-2012 and AAPL FY2009 values), so it is not usable as a PIT source.
CIK succession: current tickers map to the successor CIK (XOM -> 2115436 in 2026, which holds only 2026 facts). Predecessor CIKs must be merged. Co-registrant filings sit under only one CIK.

Ticker reuse: AGN meant Allergan Inc (850693) until 2015-03 and Allergan plc (1578845, ex-Actavis ACT) after. On Yahoo, SHLD is now 'Global X Defense Tech ETF'. Never join fundamentals to prices by ticker alone.
Yahoo, Nasdaq and Stooq have no keyless daily history for any of the 9 delisted tickers tested, so P/E and P/B for delisted names need the universe area's price source.

XBRL starts 2009-07 for large accelerated filers and mid-2011 for the rest. Comparatives reach back to 2006-2008 period ends, but they are PUBLIC only from their first XBRL filing, so a 2011 TTM may be unavailable for smaller names.

Original filings contain tagging errors that later filings fix (AGN 2013Q3 op income 970 vs 155.7M). Sanity-filter tiny monetary values; winsorize YoY and ROE, since genuine extremes exist too (JNJ FY2017 P/E ~330 after the tax-reform charge; LLTC 2011 ROE 2.13 on 506M equity; SHLD negative equity).
submissions reportDate has errors (XOM 2012-11-06 = filing date, SHLD 2001-04-30 for a 2011 10-Q, RHT 2013-07-29). Use XBRL start/end instead.
Current names also file 25-NSE (notes, exchange moves: KO 2026-09-22, WMT 2026-09-16, PG 2026-08-03). Only treat 25-NSE as delisting together with 15-12B/15-12G or an empty submissions.tickers list.
SEC requires a descriptive User-Agent with an email. Keep to 10 req/s or less per IP across all jobs (this probe used 4/s). Request gzip: companyfacts is about 7% of its size on the wire.

checks.name: pit_us_fund.py (claimed code) on the prober's 20 names: coverage reproduction

checks.issues:
Four bugs, all fixed in pit_us_fund_fixed.py.

(1) BRK-B values are wrong and nothing flags them. NI is divided by the Class-A-only dei cover count (941,481), giving ttm_eps 12,180-13,747 against a Class-B price, so P/E = 0.0067 and P/B = 0.0005 for 2011 month-ends. The same path gave V a 2010 EPS of 1.448, about 60% too high, because the cover count is class A only. Cause: when there is no diluted EPS, `implied` is NaN, so any fresh share count is accepted and then used for the ni/shares proxy.

(2) NFLX's share count is 7x too high from the 2015-07-17 event (2.98e10 vs 4.26e9), which puts P/B at 168 instead of 24.
- NFLX tags the dei cover count with the PERIOD-END context (end 2015-06-30) but reports the post-split value (426M; the 7:1 split was 2015-07-15). The code multiplies by the splits after `end`.
- The implied-count guard `abs(ttm_eps) >= 0.05` is applied on TODAY's share basis, so it is silently skipped for heavily split names: NFLX 23 of 71 events, NVDA 28 of 69, AMZN 13 of 69.
- It also accepted a 0 cover count (KO 2009-10-29).

(3) detect_splits_xbrl merges a new window only with the LAST window. TSLA got a duplicate 2020 5:1 split: (2020-02-13, 2020-10-26] n=4 plus (2020-07-28, 2021-07-27] n=2. Treated as delisted (XBRL splits), 42 of 64 TSLA events have ttm_eps off by up to 5x. The fixed detector gets 0 of 64.

(4) The claimed secnet has no get_json (separate check).

Other fragility, not code bugs:
- Per-share LEVELS (ttm_eps, bvps, shares) are on today's split basis, so they carry FUTURE split information (NFLX 2015 ttm_eps 0.044). Use only the ratios ey/bm/pe/pb as model features.
- Spin-off first filings are not XBRL. MMI's 10-K 2011-02-18 and 10-Q 2011-04-29 have isXBRL=0, so they are absent from companyfacts and nothing reports it; ttm_eps is 0% for MMI's life.
- A fiscal-year change breaks the 80-100 day quarter chain. RSH 2014 gives 9 NaN months.
- E&P revenue is tagged OilAndGasRevenue (PXD: 45 quarterly 10-Q facts before 2017), which is not in REVENUE.
- A derived Q4 absorbs a full-year-only recast. BAC's FY2025 10-K restated FY2024 revenue from 101.887 to 105.856bn, which moved the derived Q4-2024 from 25.347 to 29.316bn (+15.7%) as of 2026-02-25.
- Tagging scale errors in first filings: AGN 2013-10-31 CommonStockSharesOutstanding = 7.0 and NI/EPS implied 7.0.
- companyfacts entityName is not an identity check. CIK 70858 (BAC) returns 'BofA Finance LLC', and 826083 (old Dell) and 790070 (EMC) both return 'Dell International L.L.C.'. No post-delisting facts leaked into their series.
- HNZ 46640 keeps filing after its 2013 buyout, as Kraft Heinz Foods Co, so the panel must be cut at the delisting date.

# Full corrected module: scratch/pit/verify-us-fundamentals/pit_us_fund_fixed.py
# (= claimed pit_us_fund.py + the changes below; everything else unchanged)

EPS_BASIC = ["EarningsPerShareBasic"]  # only to sanity-check share counts when diluted EPS is absent
_WANT_GAAP = set(REVENUE + REVENUE_PARTS + NET_INCOME + OP_INCOME + EPS_DILUTED + EQUITY + NCI + SHARES_BS + SHARES_WAVG + EPS_BASIC)


def _period_implied(cf: CompanyFacts, asof: str, lo: str, splits: pd.Series | None, eps_concepts: list[str]) -> float:
    """Implied share count (today's basis) from the latest period (filed <= asof) with both NI and an
    ``eps_concepts`` EPS with |EPS as filed| >= 0.05. NI available to common preferred (TARP-era pref divs)."""
    def latest(arrs):
        best = {}
        for f in arrs:
            if "start" in f and f["filed"] <= asof and f["end"] >= lo:
                k = (f["start"], f["end"])
                if k not in best or f["filed"] > best[k]["filed"]:
                    best[k] = f
        return best
    ni = latest(cf.duration["net_income"].get("USD", []))
    ni.update(latest((cf.gaap.get("NetIncomeLossAvailableToCommonStockholdersBasic") or {}).get("USD", [])))
    eps = latest(f for c in eps_concepts for f in (cf.gaap.get(c) or {}).get("USD/shares", []))
    for k in sorted(set(ni) & set(eps), key=lambda k: (k[1], k[0]), reverse=True):
        e = eps[k]
        if abs(e["val"]) >= 0.05:
            return float(ni[k]["val"]) / (float(e["val"]) / _split_mult(pd.Timestamp(e["filed"]), splits))
    return np.nan

# --- in snapshot_features(), replace everything from `implied = ...` through the share-selection loop with:
    eps_as_filed = out["ttm_eps"] * _split_mult(d, splits)      # guard on the AS-FILED basis, not today's
    implied = out["ttm_ni"] / out["ttm_eps"] if abs(eps_as_filed) >= 0.05 else np.nan
    has_dil = any(f["filed"] <= asof and f["end"] >= lo for f in cf.duration["eps_diluted"].get("USD/shares", []))
    if not has_dil:  # BRK, V: per-class (dimensional) EPS only -> check against basic EPS
        implied = _period_implied(cf, asof, lo, splits, EPS_BASIC)
    no_check = not has_dil and np.isnan(implied)
    cands = []
    cov = pit_instant(cf, ["EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding"], asof, lo, ns="dei")
    if not cov.empty:
        r = cov.iloc[-1]
        m_end, m_filed = _split_mult(r["end"], splits), _split_mult(r["filed"], splits)
        if m_end == m_filed:
            cands.append(("dei_cover", r["val"] * m_end, r["end"]))
        elif not np.isnan(implied) and implied > 0:  # split inside (end, filed]: basis ambiguous (NFLX 2015)
            v = min((r["val"] * m for m in (m_end, m_filed)), key=lambda x: abs(np.log(x / implied)))
            cands.append(("dei_cover", v, r["end"]))
    bs = pit_instant(cf, SHARES_BS, asof, lo)
    if not bs.empty:
        r = bs.iloc[-1]
        cands.append(("bs_shares", r["val"] * _split_mult(r["filed"], splits), r["end"]))
    wa = [f for arr in (cf.gaap.get(SHARES_WAVG[0]) or {}).values() for f in arr
          if "start" in f and f["filed"] <= asof and f["end"] >= lo]
    if wa:
        f = max(wa, key=lambda x: (x["end"], x["filed"]))
        cands.append(("wavg_diluted", f["val"] * _split_mult(pd.Timestamp(f["filed"]), splits), pd.Timestamp(f["end"])))
    out["shares"], out["shares_src"] = np.nan, None
    fresh = [(s_, v_, e_) for s_, v_, e_ in cands if (d - e_).days <= 200 and v_ >= 1e4]  # drop 0 / mis-scaled
    for src, val, end in fresh:
        if no_check:  # no EPS at all -> need a second independent source within [0.67, 1.5]x
            ok = any(o != src and 0.67 <= val / ov <= 1.5 for o, ov, _ in fresh)
        else:
            ok = np.isnan(implied) or implied <= 0 or 0.67 <= val / implied <= 1.5
        if ok:
            out["shares"], out["shares_src"] = float(val), src
            break
    out["shares_implied"] = implied
    # (rest of snapshot_features unchanged: bvps, ni/shares proxy, q_derived)

# --- in detect_splits_xbrl(), replace the merge loop with:
    out: list[list] = []
    for lo_, hi_, k in sorted(ev, key=lambda x: (x[1], x[0])):  # merge with ANY overlapping same-ratio window
        for c in out:
            if c[2] == k and lo_ < c[1] and hi_ > c[0]:
                c[0], c[1], c[3] = max(c[0], lo_), min(c[1], hi_), c[3] + 1
                break
        else:
            out.append([lo_, hi_, k, 1])

checks.name: Look-ahead audit of publication dates and the PIT merge
checks.observed:
I checked all 2,165 periodic (10-K/10-Q and amendments) accns in companyfacts across the 43 names (45 CIKs).
- Every accn appears in its own submissions.
- Each accn has exactly one distinct `filed`, and companyfacts `filed` equals submissions filingDate for 2,165 of 2,165.
- acceptanceDateTime is true UTC. EDGAR index pages show the same instant in ET (AMZN 22:11:13Z = 18:11:13 ET).
- 318 accns were accepted after 17:30 ET and carry the next business day's date.
- Same-day accns: 19.4% accepted before 09:30 ET, 38.4% during the session, 42.2% after 16:00.
- Only 1 accn was accepted after its filingDate: an HNZ 10-K/A dated 2013-08-26 but accepted 2013-08-27 07:44 ET. With available = filed + 1 day that is still pre-open.
- In the fixed panels, 0 month-end rows use an event whose available date is after the month-end, or whose q_end is on or after the month-end.
- The frames API returns the latest vintage only, as claimed: JPM CY2012Q1 NI = 4,924,000,000 with accn 0000019617-13-000300, and no filed field.
- The KO 10-Q 0001628280-26-050503 (filed 2026-07-29) is still missing from companyfacts; its max filed is 2026-04-30.
checks.issues:
There is no look-ahead in the filing-date clock, and filed + 1 day is conservative for about 19% of filings, which land before the open.

The remaining look-ahead risk is in how outputs are used, not how they are built. ttm_eps, bvps and shares are expressed on TODAY's split basis, so feeding them to a model as levels leaks future splits (NFLX 2015 ttm_eps 0.044). Only ratios such as ey, bm, pe and pb are split-invariant. The panel also keeps showing a delisted name's last values for up to 200 days after its final filing, so the universe must cut it at the delisting date.

verify.final_recommendation:
Adopt the approach, but replace the claimed pit_us_fund.py with the corrected pit_us_fund_fixed.py and secnet_fixed.py. Both are in scratch/pit/verify-us-fundamentals/.

The as-of design is sound, and the prober's numbers reproduce exactly on its own sample. The filing-date clock shows no look-ahead: `filed` equals filingDate for 2,165 of 2,165 accns, every accn was accepted by `filed` + 1 day, and no panel row uses an event before it was available. Values spot-checked on 5 delisted names match reported 10-K figures.

On a different sample, however, the claimed code produced wrong values with no error, and the coverage figures overstate how well it generalizes. The four fixes:
1. Validate the NI/EPS-implied share count on the as-filed basis, and resolve cover counts when a split falls between `end` and `filed`. This fixes NFLX's 7x share count.
2. When a filer has no diluted EPS, check share counts against basic EPS or require two agreeing sources. This turns BRK-B's P/E of 0.0067 and V's 60%-off EPS into NaN.
3. Merge split windows against every same-ratio window, not just the last. This removes the duplicate TSLA split that put 42 of 64 events off by up to 5x.
4. Add get_json to secnet.

With the fixes, coverage of the prober's 20 names is unchanged, except delisted bvps goes from 99.8 to 99.6.

Constraints to plan for:
- **Multi-class filers** (BRK, V; GOOGL is partly covered): 0% per-share coverage from companyfacts. P/E and P/B for them need market-cap-level E/P and B/P built from per-class share counts from a source that keeps dimensional facts.
- **Energy E&Ps and banks:** revenue and operating-income gaps. PXD needs OilAndGasRevenue, and op_margin is 0% for BAC, CVX and PXD.
- **Spin-offs, fiscal-year changes and IPO ramps:** MMI's first filings are not XBRL; RSH's fiscal-year change blanks TTM for 9 months.
- **Full-year-only recasts:** they distort the derived Q4 (BAC Q4-2024 revenue +15.7%).
- **Features:** use only the split-invariant ratios (ey, bm, pe, pb). ttm_eps, bvps and shares are on today's split basis and carry future split information.
- **Identity:** never join by ticker. Yahoo returns a different instrument for 4 of 13 delisted tickers, and GENZ even has a full 2008-2026 history that is not Genzyme. Build the CIK chain from submissions formerNames (bulk submissions.zip), because autocomplete misses renamed shells (5 of 13 wrong first hits). Take delisting dates from the universe or price source: 25-NSE/15-12B pairs also occur for non-common securities (PIR 2017), and filers keep filing after delisting.
- **Budget:** measured companyfacts latency is about 1.0 s mean (max 4.0 s), versus the claimed 0.57 s. Allow roughly 13 minutes single-threaded for 750 CIKs; build compute is 1.2-1.4 s per company, as claimed.
